established_findings.statement: Large language models (LLMs) are being actively applied and proposed for NetOps tasks including intent-to-configuration translation, intent-driven management, automation, and zero-touch configuration.
limitations: Many records are surveys, frameworks, or proofs-of-concept rather than large-scale production deployments
Work spans 2024–2026; practical maturity varies by study

established_findings.statement: Hallucination and factual/constraint violations by LLMs are a well-documented reliability problem that threatens trustworthiness of LLM-generated operational artifacts.
limitations: Most evidence documents hallucination at task- or document-level; operational impact depends on downstream validators and deployment context

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented architectures (LLMs calling deterministic validators/tools or using RAG/tool planners) are proposed and empirically shown to improve factual grounding or task success, but introduce performance, engineering, and system-design tradeoffs.
limitations: Improvements reported vary by task and metric; extra latency and complexity are frequently noted
Many results are from controlled evaluations rather than large production rollouts

established_findings.statement: Network verification and simulator tools (e.g., Batfish / formal verification approaches) are common components proposed as validators in LLM-driven NetOps pipelines.
limitations: Some references are system proposals or tech reports that describe integration with Batfish rather than large-scale empirical validation

established_findings.statement: Benchmarks and public datasets aimed at NetOps/AIOps evaluation are emerging (e.g., NetConfEval, ClosRCA-Bench, OPNet-Sim), enabling reproducible evaluation but with ongoing concerns about construct and external validity.
limitations: Benchmarks vary in scope; many are synthetic or topology-limited, raising external-validity questions

established_findings.statement: Studies in adjacent domains (code translation, SOC RAG pipelines) show concrete failure modes (translation bugs, adversarially induced hallucinations) that are relevant threats to NetOps agent pipelines.
limitations: Extrapolation from adjacent domains is suggestive but not direct evidence of identical failure rates in NetOps

unresolved_questions.statement: How effective are generate–validate–repair (or generate–verify–repair) loops at preventing unsafe or incorrect network configurations across diverse, realistic topologies and at production scale?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: proposed architectures and benchmarks (no large-scale conclusive empirical results)
limitations: Existing works propose and evaluate such loops in controlled or limited settings; large-scale operational evidence is not provided in supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: What are the operational latency, availability, and reliability tradeoffs when LLMs call external validators/tools in time-sensitive NetOps workflows?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: tool-augmented LLM studies and systems analyses
limitations: Some studies analyze queuing/control or latency in tool-augmented settings but not specifically for large-scale NetOps SLAs

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do existing NetOps benchmarks measure the operational safety constructs that matter in production (reachability, policy compliance, loop-freedom) versus proxy or superficial criteria?
limitations: Benchmarks exist but supplied records do not establish comprehensive construct-validity analyses

unresolved_questions.statement: How transferable are mitigations (constrained decoding, IPCD, tool-planning, provenance flags) from other domains to preventing actionable misconfigurations in NetOps?
limitations: Methods have been validated in non-NetOps domains or limited NetOps proofs-of-concept in the supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: What are the realistic attack surfaces and practical effectiveness of adversarial poisoning or hallucination-engineering attacks against NetOps RAG pipelines?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: adversarial and hallucination studies in related domains
limitations: Adversarial SOC/RAG experiments are documented; direct NetOps-targeted adversarial experiments are not present in the supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: Lack of large-scale, topology-grounded empirical studies that measure rates of actionable misconfiguration from LLM-driven pipelines under realistic operational constraints.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: gap inferred from benchmarks and survey coverage
limitations: Some narrow or synthetic benchmarks exist, but no supplied record shows broad production-scale measurement

candidate_gaps.statement: Insufficient validated evaluations of generate–validate–repair pipelines that jointly measure safety (policy compliance, reachability), operator workload, and system latency.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: methodology and tool papers lacking joint operational metrics
limitations: Papers propose components but do not present comprehensive joint-metric evaluations in the supplied set

candidate_gaps.statement: Need for NetOps-specific adversarial and robustness benchmarks that quantify how RAG and tool-augmented pipelines respond to poisoned retrievals or crafted prompts.
limitations: Adversarial experiments exist in SOC contexts; NetOps-specific datasets and attacks are not present in supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: Limited evidence on human-in-the-loop oversight efficacy in fast NetOps change workflows: how operator review integrates with automated validators under realistic cognitive and time pressures.
limitations: HITL literature discusses conceptual and cross-domain issues; operational NetOps studies under real conditions are not present

candidate_gaps.statement: Construct-validity gap in existing NetOps benchmarks: need to verify that benchmark success correlates with reduction of operational incidents in deployments.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: benchmark papers and inferred methodological critique
limitations: Some benchmarks are new and synthetic; supplied records do not report deployment-to-incident correlation studies

excluded_claims: LLMs are proven production-ready to autonomously perform NetOps changes without human oversight (unsupported by supplied records).
There is evidence of absence of hallucination or factual errors in LLM outputs for NetOps (supplied records document hallucination risk rather than its nonexistence).
Any single paper in the supplied set demonstrates comprehensive, large-scale production validation of agentic NetOps across heterogeneous real networks (no supplied record provides that).
Claims of having eliminated adversarial or poisoning risks for RAG-based NetOps pipelines are unsupported by the supplied records.
